item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Aug 30, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: River Run + Cold Plunge (with Sauna!) — Tue Sep 1, 3:00 PM — The Floathouse Petaluma
item.description: Trade your Saturday afternoon for a tidal adventure on the Petaluma River. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this guided Downriver Run takes you six scenic miles through wide-open wetlands and peaceful river landscapes in easy-to-use Hobie pedal kayaks. From 3–5 pm, ride the outgoing tide from The Floathouse Petaluma to Lakeville Landing Marina, where the experience can continue with an optional discounted sauna + cold plunge session at Sundrop Sauna from 5–6:30 pm. Warm up in the sauna, cool down with a plunge, and relax riverside in the golden evening light. Want to make it a floating picnic party? Add a Bella Box from La Bella Charcuterie, with omnivore, vegetarian, and vegan options available. This is Sonoma County river culture at its finest: movement, nature, community, wellness, and good vibes — all in one unforgettable afternoon. Join Sonoma County Women Professionals on Tuesday, September 1 for an inspiring and practical presentation with Michelle Maree, speaking and visibility coach, trauma-trained therapist, and somatic guide. Michelle will share practical, evidence-based tools to help you: • Communicate with greater confidence and clarity • Stay grounded in high-pressure situations • Regulate your nervous system when the stakes are high • Navigate challenging conversations with authenticity • Turn pressure into an opportunity for greater connection and influence Whether you’re presenting to an audience, networking, leading a team, or simply looking to show up more confidently, you’ll leave with tools you can use in both business and life. item.description: The September 3 Wake Up with the Metro Chamber event will focus on homelessness as one of the region's most significant economic, public safety, humanitarian, and quality-of-life challenges. item.title: Common Ground Book Club: books by & about people with disabilities — Fri Sep 4, 10:30 AM — Sebastopol Library
item.description:
Meet with others to discuss books centering disability voices! Copies of each month's books are available at the Sonoma County Library Catalog. Pre-Register to receive a reminder email. Drop-ins are welcome. If you didn't have time to read or finish the month's book, you are still welcome to attend. Snacks will be provided. Common Ground Society serves families who have loved ones with any sort of unique need while also educating our community on how to be inclusive. Held the 1st Friday of the month from 10:30-11:30am. We will not be meeting in January. 12/05/2025- December's title is Unfit Parent : A Disabled Mother Challenges An Inaccessible World by Jessica Slice 2/06/2025- Disability Intimacy: Essays on Love, Care, and Desire: Edited by Alice Wong 3/06/2025- The Kiss Quotient by Helen Hoang 04/03/2025- True Biz by Sara Nović 05/01/2025- Second Life: Having a Child in the Digital Age by Amanda Hess
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Frank Lloyd Wright Civic Center Tours — Fri Sep 4, 10:30 AM — Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Adult $10, Senior/Full Time Student $5 \(Plus a $2 p er ticket service Charge Online\)
Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.description:
A showcase of the local maker community – live music, interactive projects, demos, wine and beer, & more. Chimera Arts, Sonoma County’s maker space, continues their First Fridays at Chimera Arts, a showcase of our local maker community. There will be live music, food and beverages, activities and live demonstrations. Old Caz beer, gourmet hot dogs, live music and demonstrations, and hands-on activities. See you there! Chimera Arts is Sonoma County’s only community arts and makerspace, located in downtown Sebastopol at the old Ford Garage building. We’re a community of makers that offer classes, expertise and equipment to anyone interested in bringing their creative ideas to life.
